title: At the Airport
goal: Ask for help through an airport journey, understand key crew language, and give arrival information.

runs.text: A
boarding pass
identifies your flight and boarding details.
Check-in
confirms your travel booking;
bag drop
is where a checked bag is accepted.
Carry-on
means baggage carried into the cabin.
Gate
is the departure boarding point;
baggage claim
is the arrival area for checked bags. These terms do not tell you an airline's exact baggage rules.

turns.speaker: Agent

runs.text: Where are you flying today?

turns.en: Where are you flying today?

turns.speaker: Traveler

runs.text: Denver, on Flight 246. Is it on time?

turns.en: Denver, on Flight 246. Is it on time?

turns.speaker: Agent

runs.text: At the moment, yes. Are you checking a bag?

turns.en: At the moment, yes. Are you checking a bag?

turns.speaker: Traveler

runs.text: One suitcase. Where's the bag drop?

turns.en: One suitcase. Where's the bag drop?

turns.speaker: Agent

runs.text: At the counter to your left.

turns.en: At the counter to your left.

turns.speaker: Traveler

runs.text: Could I have an aisle seat if one is available?

turns.en: Could I have an aisle seat if one is available?

turns.speaker: Agent

runs.text: I'll check. The window seat is still available, too.

turns.en: I'll check. The window seat is still available, too.

blocks.caption: Check-in and bag drop · Agent & Traveler

runs.text: Ask “What's the baggage allowance for this ticket?” “Is there a fee for this bag?” and “Where is the check-in counter?” A
window seat
is beside the window; an
aisle seat
is beside the passage. “Any chance of an upgrade?” is a conversational request, not a claim to an upgrade.
Procedures vary. Use “What do I need to take out?” or “Could you show me where this goes?” to follow the instructions for your actual checkpoint.
Tray / bin
names a container;
scanner
names equipment used for screening.

turns.speaker: Traveler

runs.text: Excuse me, which gate is Flight 246 using?

turns.en: Excuse me, which gate is Flight 246 using?

turns.speaker: Employee

runs.text: Gate C12. Boarding starts at 2:20.

turns.en: Gate C12. Boarding starts at 2:20.

turns.speaker: Traveler

runs.text: What time does boarding close?

turns.en: What time does boarding close?

turns.speaker: Employee

runs.text: For this flight, 2:45.

turns.en: For this flight, 2:45.

turns.speaker: Traveler

runs.text: The screen now says delayed. Has the gate changed?

turns.en: The screen now says delayed. Has the gate changed?

turns.speaker: Employee

runs.text: It's still C12. Please check the updated departure information.

turns.en: It's still C12. Please check the updated departure information.

blocks.caption: Security and the gate · Traveler & Employee

runs.text: A delay, a boarding time, and a gate-closing time are different details. Ask about each rather than treating departure time as the whole plan.

turns.speaker: Crew member

runs.text: May I see your boarding pass?

turns.en: May I see your boarding pass?

turns.speaker: Traveler

runs.text: Here it is. I'm in 18C. Which way is that?

turns.en: Here it is. I'm in 18C. Which way is that?

turns.speaker: Crew member

runs.text: Down the aisle, on your left.

turns.en: Down the aisle, on your left.

turns.speaker: Traveler

runs.text: Could you help me with this bag?

turns.en: Could you help me with this bag?

turns.speaker: Crew member

runs.text: Sure. Let's find space in the overhead bin.

turns.en: Sure. Let's find space in the overhead bin.

blocks.caption: Boarding and the cabin · Crew member & Traveler

runs.text: Useful cabin words:
row
, a line of seats;
seat belt
, the strap securing you in a seat;
tray table
, the small folding table;
reading light
, the light above your seat;
life vest
, emergency flotation equipment.
Turbulence
describes irregular air movement that can make a flight bumpy.

These model crew instructions teach meaning: “Please fasten your seat belt.” “Return your seat to the upright position.” “Stow your tray table.” “Switch your device to airplane mode.” Follow the actual crew's instructions; these examples are not a complete flight-safety procedure.

turns.speaker: Traveler

runs.text: Could I have some water, please?

turns.en: Could I have some water, please?

turns.speaker: Crew member

runs.text: Of course.

turns.en: Of course.

turns.speaker: Traveler

runs.text: I'm feeling unwell. Could you help me?

turns.en: I'm feeling unwell. Could you help me?

turns.speaker: Crew member

runs.text: I'll come over.

turns.en: I'll come over.

blocks.caption: Boarding and the cabin · Traveler & Crew member

turns.speaker: Officer

runs.text: What's the purpose of your visit?

turns.en: What's the purpose of your visit?

turns.speaker: Visitor

runs.text: I'm visiting friends for ten days.

turns.en: I'm visiting friends for ten days.

turns.speaker: Officer

runs.text: Where are you staying?

turns.en: Where are you staying?

turns.speaker: Visitor

runs.text: At their home in Portland. I have the address here.

turns.en: At their home in Portland. I have the address here.

blocks.caption: Arrival: a separate international visit · Officer & Visitor

runs.text: Use information that describes your actual trip. If necessary, say “Could you repeat the question?” Immigration and customs requirements depend on your journey; this exchange is language practice, not entry-policy advice.

turns.speaker: Traveler

runs.text: Which carousel is our flight's baggage on?

turns.en: Which carousel is our flight's baggage on?

turns.speaker: Employee

runs.text: Carousel 5.

turns.en: Carousel 5.

turns.speaker: Traveler

runs.text: My suitcase hasn't arrived. Where can I report it?

turns.en: My suitcase hasn't arrived. Where can I report it?

turns.speaker: Employee

runs.text: At the airline's baggage service desk.

turns.en: At the airline's baggage service desk.

blocks.caption: Arrival: a separate international visit · Traveler & Employee

runs.text: An
airport cart

carries luggage. At the rental counter: “I have a reservation under Maya Lee.” Staff may ask for documents. Ask “What documents do you need?” and “Where do I return the car?” For money exchange, ask “What's the exchange rate, and are there any fees?” For a pickup, ask “Where's the designated pickup area?”

Fictional travel card: Flight 246 to Denver; gate C12; boarding 2:20; closes 2:45; one suitcase; aisle seat requested; arrival carousel 5. Separate international visitor role: arriving in Portland from abroad, for ten days with friends.
Make the check-in request. Partner says the aisle seat is unavailable. Accept the window seat or ask about another option.
Ask about the gate and boarding times. Partner uses the card. Repeat the three details in your own words.
Report missing baggage. Partner asks “Which flight were you on?” Supply the number and ask where to make the report.
Answer the arrival questions using the visitor role. Change the trip purpose to a vacation if desired, without inventing a visa rule.
Alone, read each staff question and answer out loud; then cover the card and reconstruct the journey.
Possibilities:

“The window seat is fine.” “Flight 246. My suitcase isn't on Carousel 5.” “I'm visiting friends for ten days.” Check whether the other person can identify your flight, need, and next question. Policies and times in this lesson are fictional.
